intro_content: The internal audit charter is a fundamental regulatory document that defines the general framework of the internal audit activity in electronic payment companies. It clarifies its purpose, authorities, and responsibilities in accordance with good corporate governance requirements and approved professional standards for internal auditing, and in compliance with laws and instructions issued by competent regulatory authorities and instructions from the company’s senior management.

Given the sensitive and complex nature of electronic payment operations, and the operational, technical, financial, and information security risks they encompass, the internal audit charter aims to enhance the independence and objectivity of the internal audit activity. It ensures its ability to provide independent objective assurances and consulting to senior management regarding the adequacy and effectiveness of internal control systems, risk management, and compliance with applicable policies, regulations, and instructions. This charter also helps support confidence in electronic payment systems, protect customer funds and data, achieve compliance with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing requirements, and ensure the integrity and continuity of operations, thereby bolstering the company's stability and reputation in the financial market.

The charter also establishes the right of access to all relevant financial, administrative, and legal matters necessary to perform audit assignments. It further aims to clarify independence and professional integrity requirements for department employees. Final approval of the charter falls under the authority of senior management.

This charter is deemed to be a formal reference governing the relationship of the internal audit activity with senior management and specialized committees, forming a basis for performing its duties according to the best professional practices and international standards for internal auditing.

definitions_items.def: The supreme body responsible for shaping the company's general policies, overseeing executive management, and approving the internal audit charter and its plans.
An official document approved by senior management that defines the purpose, authority, responsibility, and relationship of the internal audit activity with other entities within the company.

An independent and objective assurance and consulting activity designed to add value and improve the company’s operations by evaluating and enhancing the effectiveness of risk management, internal control, governance, and the policies and procedures established by management to ensure the achievement of operational and financial objectives, protection of assets, data reliability, and compliance with laws and instructions.
An official document containing the results of audit work, observations, recommendations, and proposed corrective action plans.

charter.organization_title: Second: Organization and Functional Reporting Lines
organization_content: The department is positioned within the organizational structure to achieve the highest levels of independence and objectivity in performing its duties, working impartially without bias, interference, or conflict of interest per internal audit standards. The independence of the internal audit activity is achieved through its relationship and reporting line within the organization's structure, as well as the objectivity of internal auditors during their work. To attain the necessary degree of independence for effective performance, the department reports directly to the Managing Director. The department manager manages the internal audit activity, supervises its work, and is responsible to management in the capacity of department manager.

Company management is aware that the presence of an internal audit activity does not substitute an effective internal control and governance system; rather, it aids in maintaining effective control policies and procedures by testing and evaluating their efficiency and competence in mitigating risks across all aspects of governance, operations, and information systems.
charter.purpose_title: Third: Purpose of Internal Audit Activity
purpose_content: The internal audit activity aims to provide independent and objective assurance and consulting services. It contributes to improving operational efficiency and supporting the achievement of the company's strategic objectives, not merely discovering deficiencies, through a systematic and organized methodology to evaluate and improve the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and control processes through (Procedures - Audit Manual - Annual Audit Plan). It assists in:
1. Enhancing the reliability and integrity of electronic payment systems.
2. Evaluating the effectiveness of internal control systems and risk management.
3. Ensuring compliance with regulatory laws and requirements for anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing.
reports_content: The department prepares regular or special reports reflecting the nature of its work, aiding in decision-making within the company, and ensuring compliance with organizational and administrative requirements. These include performance analyses, follow-up reports, or statistical data submitted to senior management or relevant authorities. These reports aim to document workflow, identify challenges, and provide recommendations to improve operations. The following table showcases the key reports prepared by the department:

independence_content: The Internal Audit Department shall be independent, and internal auditors shall perform their work objectively. To achieve administrative support and independence effectively, the following must be observed:
1. Department employees report only to the department management.

2. The department is independent from the activities it audits. The internal audit activity in the company shall not hold any authority or responsibility over internal operational activities (e.g., internal auditors shall not assume any executive duties or tasks they might audit later, ensuring task rotation among department staff).

3. The department manager is authorized to communicate directly with the Managing Director, the external auditor, the compliance officer in the company, and any other administrative level required for audit duties.
4. Budget limitations and any related considerations imposed by administrative reporting lines should not impede the department's ability to fulfill its duties.
5. The administrative reporting line for the department should be higher than the authority or scope of the department's work.

6. Administrative reporting must be adequate to facilitate direct communication with executive management and department heads. The department must have unrestricted direct access to any administrative level to help precise bidirectional information flow, meaning that information regarding actions and plans should be provided to the department manager and audit teams in a timely manner.

7. Internal auditors must act with objectivity, neutrality, and unbiased attitudes. No restrictions on the scope of work or the auditor's conduct may significantly influence their opinions concerning internal audit reports or lead to conclusions not supported by evidence.
8. Department employees' performance evaluations for promotions and bonuses shall not be subject to any lower administrative levels.

9. The department's work shall not be subject to any form of restriction, whether by limiting its scope, restricting communication with various management levels, blocking access to information, reports, or documents, preventing entry into certain areas or units, delaying the delivery of necessary data, or imposing financial constraints impeding task execution.
10. The department must establish standard operating procedures applicable across all audited departments.
charter.scope_title: Seventh: Scope of Internal Audit Work
scope_content: The scope of internal audit work covers all company activities and units without exception, specifically:
1. Financial and accounting operations and reconciliations.
2. Electronic payment and collection operations, wallet and card management.
3. Information systems, technology, cybersecurity, and business continuity.
4. Adherence to CBI and other regulatory authority requirements.
5. Monitoring customer data privacy and information confidentiality.
6. Monitoring external service providers and agents subject to risk-levels.
authorities_content: The internal audit activity is granted the following full authorities:

1. Management authorizes the department—to carry out the tasks listed in item nine—to communicate with any employee in the company, review and audit any file, activity, document, review committee meeting minutes, access camera records, and have unrestricted access to units, workspaces, data centers, and storage facilities to carry out monitoring and auditing activities.
2. Unrestricted access to all records, data, electronic systems, and databases.
3. The department manager has the authority to form audit teams for field visits to company departments, branches, offices, and agents according to the pre-approved plan by management.
4. Rely on corporate information systems and their suitability to operations and required information, including reports demanded by the CBI.
5. Employ specialized personnel and administrative auditors with sufficient experience to cover specialized audit tasks (internal or external) when necessary upon management approval.
6. View contracts and agreements with banks, service providers, and merchants.
7. Conduct interviews with employees and management as needed without prior notice.
charter.responsibilities_title: Ninth: Roles and Responsibilities of the Department
responsibilities_content: The responsibilities of the internal audit activity, distributed according to the department's structure, include the following:
1. Prepare an annual risk-based audit plan and attain management approval.
2. Control and supervise other company departments through follow-ups to ensure tasks are completed according to established policies and procedures.
3. Execute audit tasks according to professional standards and to suit the nature of electronic payment activities.
4. Evaluate the effectiveness of controls relating to payment systems, cybersecurity, and business continuity.
5. Prepare quarterly and semi-annual reports encompassing observations, risks, and recommendations to the relevant authorities.
6. Follow up on the implementation of recommendations and the remediation of regulatory findings.
7. Review expense procedures and evaluate adherence to them.
8. Maintain the confidentiality of customer information and sensitive data.
9. Audit IT and communications following the IT corporate governance guidelines prescribed by the CBI through highly skilled and expert personnel.
10. Set audit programs focusing on the competencies and numbers of staff available.
Note: The internal audit department does not participate in the design or implementation of controls they must later evaluate.
charter.manager_responsibilities_title: Tenth: Duties and Responsibilities of the Department Manager
manager_responsibilities_content: The duties of the department manager, within approved resources, to ensure performance measurement are exclusively as follows:
1. Establish a comprehensive strategy for the internal audit activity in line with electronic payment operations.
2. Prepare and update the internal audit charter for board approval.
3. Build a risk-based audit methodology.
4. Support corporate governance and foster a culture of compliance and control.
5. Determine audit priorities across electronic payments, systems, cybersecurity, and compliance.
6. Supervise the execution of audit tasks and ensure quality within approved schedules.
7. Review and approve audit assignment programs and working papers.
8. Oversee the auditing of electronic payment systems, portfolios, and cards.
9. Evaluate the effectiveness of technical controls, information security, and access management.
10. Monitor business continuity and disaster recovery testings.
11. Coordinate with IT teams in addressing technical vulnerabilities and risks.
12. Guarantee compliance with CBI and related regulatory authorities instructions.
13. Track the implementation of AML/CFT requirements.
14. Review regulatory reports and verify the remediation of observations set within them.
15. Collaborate with compliance and risk management units without compromising audit independence.
16. Submit periodic internal audit reports to senior management and the audit committee.
17. Present material observations and high risks along with corrective recommendations based on the risk appetite approved by senior management.
18. Follow up on recommendations, remediation plans, and periodic escalations regarding delays.
19. Lead and develop the internal audit team.
20. Assign tasks and evaluate the performance of internal auditors.
21. Identify training needs and capacity building in e-payment and technical auditing fields.
22. Adhere to professional ethics and standards.
charter.external_relations_title: Eleventh: Relations with Regulatory Authorities and External Audit
external_relations_content: 1. The internal audit activity cooperates with the external auditor and regulatory bodies, including the CBI, to ensure effort integration and avoid duplication.
2. The internal audit activity commits to providing regulatory authorities with required reports and information within the legal frameworks.
references_content: 1. International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing
3. Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) instructions and requirements
4. Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing standards
5. Information security frameworks and best practices (e.g., COBIT)
7. Banking Law No. (94) of 2004 and its amendments.
9. Licensing and regulating electronic payment companies instructions issued by the CBI.
10. Corporate governance instructions for banks and non-banking financial institutions issued by the CBI.
11. Internal control and risk management instructions issued by the CBI.
12. AML/CFT instructions No. (1) of 2016 and its amendments.
14. Customer data protection and bank secrecy instructions issued by the CBI.
15. Cybersecurity, business continuity, and disaster recovery instructions issued by the CBI.
16. Regulation No. (2) of (2024) / CBI / Circular No. (240/4/9) dated (15/5/2024).
approval_content: 1. This charter is approved by senior management.
2. The charter is reviewed periodically or upon the issuance of new regulatory instructions, and is updated to conform to the nature of electronic payment operations.

charter_intro_content: The Internal Audit Charter is a formal document that defines the internal audit activity's purpose, authority, and responsibility.
The internal audit activity is established by the Board of Directors. The internal audit activity's responsibilities are defined by the Board as part of their oversight role.

charter_definitions_items.def: An independent, objective assurance and consulting activity designed to add value and improve an organization's operations.
The highest level governing body (e.g., Board of Directors) responsible for directing and overseeing the organization.

charter_organization_content: The Internal Audit Manager reports functionally to the Board and administratively to the CEO.
The Board approves the internal audit charter, the risk-based internal audit plan, and the internal audit budget.
charter_purpose_content: The purpose of the internal audit activity is to provide independent, objective assurance and consulting services designed to add value and improve Al-Saqi's operations.
charter_reports_content: The internal audit activity reports the results of its work to the Board and senior management.

charter_reports_table.name: Quarterly Report
charter_reports_table.notes: Summary of activities and plan progress

charter_independence_content: The internal audit activity will remain free from interference by any element in the organization, including matters of audit selection, scope, procedures, frequency, timing, or report content.
charter_scope_content: The scope of internal audit activities encompasses, but is not limited to, objective examinations of evidence for the purpose of providing independent assessments.
charter_authorities_content: The internal audit activity, with strict accountability for confidentiality and safeguarding records and information, is authorized full, free, and unrestricted access to any and all of Al-Saqi's records, physical properties, and personnel pertinent to carrying out any engagement.
charter_responsibilities_content: Develop and implement a flexible annual audit plan using an appropriate risk-based methodology.
charter_manager_responsibilities_content: Ensure the internal audit activity has sufficient, appropriate, and relevant resources.
charter_external_relations_content: Coordinate with and provide oversight of other control and monitoring functions.
charter_references_content: International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) of the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA).
charter_approval_content: This charter was approved by the Board of Directors on the date indicated below.
